aleurone-layer.alt: Aleurone Layer: close macro of a wheat kernel showing its layers
aleurone-layer.caption: Close macro of a wheat kernel showing its layers.

aliquot-jar.alt: Aliquot Jar: dough sample in a straight-sided jar beside the bulk dough
aliquot-jar.caption: A small straight-sided sample of dough that shows the true percentage rise.

ancient-grain.alt: Ancient Grain: several actual grain varieties side by side (einkorn, emmer, spelt, rye)
ancient-grain.caption: Several actual grain varieties side by side (einkorn, emmer, spelt, rye).

ascorbic-acid.alt: A bottle labeled Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C), a dough-strengthening ingredient used in small amounts in bread baking
ascorbic-acid.caption: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C; in bread formulas it is used in very small amounts as a dough strengthener.

autolyse.alt: Autolyse: flour and water just mixed into a rough shaggy dough, unkneaded
autolyse.caption: Flour and water, rested before salt and leaven go in.

babka.alt: Babka: chocolate babka, sliced to show the swirl
babka.caption: Chocolate babka, sliced to show the swirl.

baguette.alt: Baguette: finished baguette, cut to show the crumb
baguette.caption: A long, thin loaf with a crackly crust, scored on the diagonal.

bakers-couche.alt: Long bread dough pieces proofing in the folds of a baker's couche
bakers-couche.caption: A baker's couche supports long loaves in fabric folds so they hold their shape while proofing.

bakers-percentage.alt: Baker's Percentage: kitchen scale with flour and water, simple weights visible
bakers-percentage.caption: Every ingredient expressed as a percent of the flour, which is always 100%.

baking-steel.alt: A baker holding a rectangular Baking Steel plate above a wooden work surface
baking-steel.caption: A solid steel plate provides a preheated baking surface for bread.

banneton.alt: Banneton: dough proofing in a rattan banneton basket
banneton.caption: The coiled basket that supports the dough during its final rise.

bassinage.alt: Bassinage: held-back water being worked into dough
bassinage.caption: Held-back water being worked into dough.

batard.caption: An oval loaf, shorter and fatter than a baguette.

bench-rest.alt: Bench Rest: pre-shaped dough rounds resting uncovered on a bench
bench-rest.caption: Pre-shaped dough rounds resting uncovered on a bench.

bench-scraper.alt: Bench Scraper: metal bench scraper being used with bread dough
bench-scraper.caption: A flat blade for dividing, lifting and shaping dough on the counter.

bialy.alt: Bialy: bialy with onion and poppy seed topping
bialy.caption: Bialy with onion and poppy seed topping.

biga.alt: Biga: mature stiff biga preferment showing structure
biga.caption: Mature stiff biga preferment showing structure.

blowout.alt: Blowout: loaf showing a side or bottom blowout burst
blowout.caption: The crust bursts where it was not scored, because the gas found its own exit.

bolted-flour.alt: Bolted Flour: whole flour beside sifted/bolted flour for comparison
bolted-flour.caption: Whole flour beside sifted/bolted flour for comparison.

bolting.alt: Bolting: hands sifting fresh-milled flour through a sieve
bolting.caption: Hands sifting fresh-milled flour through a sieve.

boule.caption: A round loaf, from the French word for ball.

braiding.alt: Braiding: hands braiding challah dough strands
braiding.caption: Outside strand over the middle, alternating sides.

bran-soaker.alt: Dry wheat bran beside hydrated bran after soaking
bran-soaker.caption: Dry bran next to bran after soaking. Pre-hydrated bran softens and competes less with gluten.

bulk-fermentation.alt: Bulk Fermentation: dough fermenting in a clear container with visible bubbles
bulk-fermentation.caption: The first rise, measured by how much the whole mass grows.

ciabatta.alt: Ciabatta: ciabatta CUT OPEN showing the open crumb (interior shot required)
ciabatta.caption: Ciabatta CUT OPEN showing the open crumb (interior shot required).

coil-fold.alt: Coil Fold: hands performing a coil fold on dough
coil-fold.caption: Lift from the middle so both ends hang, then let them tuck under as you set it down.

cold-proof.alt: Cold Proof: shaped dough in a banneton going into a refrigerator
cold-proof.caption: A long, cold final rise in the fridge builds flavor and makes scoring easier.

crumb.alt: Crumb: sliced loaf showing an open crumb structure
crumb.caption: The inside of the loaf: its holes, texture and tenderness.

dense-crumb.alt: Dense Crumb: sliced loaf with a dense tight crumb
dense-crumb.caption: Tight and heavy, usually from too little fermentation or weak gluten.

digital-scale.alt: Digital Scale: bread ingredients being weighed in grams on a digital scale
digital-scale.caption: Weigh everything in grams. Cups are a guess.

dutch-oven.alt: Dutch Oven: loaf baking inside a Dutch oven with the lid off
dutch-oven.caption: A heavy lidded pot that traps steam from the dough itself.

ear.alt: Ear: close-up of a sourdough ear, the raised crispy flap along the score
ear.caption: The raised flap of crust along the score, lifted by oven spring.

endosperm.alt: Endosperm: wheat kernel cross-section showing the endosperm
endosperm.caption: Wheat kernel cross-section showing the endosperm.

english-muffin.alt: English Muffin: English muffin split showing the crumb
english-muffin.caption: English muffin split showing the crumb.

float-test.alt: Float Test: spoonful of starter floating in a glass of water
float-test.caption: A spoonful that floats is full of gas. One that sinks may still be ready.

flying-crust.alt: Flying Crust: sliced loaf with the crust separated from the crumb (the flying-crust defect)
flying-crust.caption: The top crust separates and lifts away from the crumb below it.

fools-crumb.alt: Fool's Crumb: sliced loaf with large tunnels surrounded by dense crumb (underfermented)
fools-crumb.caption: A few giant holes with dense crumb around them: underfermented, not open.

gluten.alt: Gluten: dough stretched to show a developed gluten network
gluten.caption: The stretchy protein network that traps gas and gives bread its structure.

grain-mill.caption: Turns whole wheat berries into fresh flour at home.

gummy-crumb.alt: Gummy Crumb: close-up of a gummy wet crumb interior
gummy-crumb.caption: A wet, sticky band, often from cutting too soon or underbaking.

hard-red-spring-wheat.alt: Hard Red Spring Wheat: red wheat berries plus flour
hard-red-spring-wheat.caption: Red wheat berries plus flour.

hard-red-winter-wheat.alt: Hard Red Winter Wheat: red wheat berries plus flour
hard-red-winter-wheat.caption: Red wheat berries plus flour.

hard-white-wheat.alt: Hard White Wheat: white wheat berries plus flour
hard-white-wheat.caption: White wheat berries plus flour.

hydration.alt: Lower- and higher-hydration bread dough shown side by side
hydration.caption: Water as a percentage of flour weight. 750 g water on 1,000 g flour is 75%.

kneading.caption: Working the dough by hand to build gluten strength.

lame.caption: A razor blade on a handle, made for scoring dough.

lamination.alt: Lamination: dough stretched thin across a work surface
lamination.caption: Alternating layers of dough and butter, folded over and over.

letter-fold.alt: Letter Fold: dough at the letter-fold stage
letter-fold.caption: Dough at the letter-fold stage.

levain.alt: Levain: mature levain at peak, risen in its container
levain.caption: Mature levain at peak, risen in its container.

milk-bread.alt: Milk Bread (Shokupan): Japanese milk bread loaf
milk-bread.caption: Japanese milk bread loaf.

oven-spring.alt: Oven Spring: baked loaf showing strong oven-spring rise
oven-spring.caption: The fast rise in the first minutes of baking, before the crust sets.

oven-steam.alt: Steam (Baking): steam in the oven or a steaming setup for bread baking
oven-steam.caption: Steam keeps the crust soft long enough for the loaf to finish expanding.

overproofed.alt: Overproofed: overproofed dough or a flat overproofed loaf
overproofed.caption: Risen past its peak. The gluten is tired and the loaf will sink or spread.

pancaking.alt: Pancaking: loaf spreading flat after being turned out of the banneton
pancaking.caption: The loaf spreads sideways in the oven instead of rising up.

particle-size.alt: Coarse, medium, and fine fresh-milled flour particle sizes shown side by side
particle-size.caption: Coarse, medium, and fine fresh-milled flour. Finer flour takes up water faster; coarser flour adds texture.

pita.alt: Pita: pita bread showing the pocket
pita.caption: Pita bread showing the pocket.

poke-test.alt: Poke Test: finger pressing proofed dough leaving a visible indentation
poke-test.caption: A floured finger dent that fills back slowly is a loaf ready to bake.

pre-shape.alt: Pre-Shape: dough being pre-shaped into a round
pre-shape.caption: A loose round first lets the dough relax before the final shape.

probe-thermometer.alt: Probe Thermometer: instant-read thermometer inserted into a finished loaf
probe-thermometer.caption: Read the inside temperature to know the loaf is actually done.

proofing.alt: Proofing: shaped dough visibly risen in a banneton, final proof
proofing.caption: The final rise after shaping, right before the oven.

rubaud-method.alt: Rubaud Method: hand doing Rubaud mixing in a bowl
rubaud-method.caption: Hand doing Rubaud mixing in a bowl.

rye-flour.alt: Rye Flour: rye berries and freshly milled rye flour
rye-flour.caption: Rye berries and freshly milled rye flour.

scoring.alt: Scoring: hands scoring sourdough dough with a lame
scoring.caption: A shallow cut at a low angle tells the loaf where to open.

shaping.caption: Tension on the surface, seam on the bottom. That skin is what holds the rise.

sifter.alt: Sifter: flour sieve/sifter with flour and retained bran
sifter.caption: Flour sieve/sifter with flour and retained bran.

slap-and-fold.alt: Slap and Fold: dough in the slap-and-fold motion
slap-and-fold.caption: Lift, slap the far end down, fold the rest over. Wet dough tightens fast this way.

sourdough-starter.caption: A living culture of flour, water, wild yeast and bacteria that leavens bread.

stiff-starter.alt: Stiff Starter: firm stiff starter beside a regular liquid starter
stiff-starter.caption: Firm stiff starter beside a regular liquid starter.

stitching.alt: Stitching: a batard being stitched while in the banneton
stitching.caption: A batard being stitched while in the banneton.

stone-mill.alt: Stone Mill: an actual stone grain mill
stone-mill.caption: An actual stone grain mill.

stretch-and-fold.alt: Stretch and Fold: hands performing a stretch and fold
stretch-and-fold.caption: Grab one side, stretch it up, and fold it over the top. Turn the bowl and repeat.

surface-tension.alt: Surface Tension: a properly shaped tight smooth boule
surface-tension.caption: A properly shaped tight smooth boule.

tangzhong.alt: Tangzhong: cooked tangzhong paste showing a pudding-like consistency
tangzhong.caption: A cooked flour paste that holds extra water for a softer, longer-lasting crumb.

tunneling.alt: Tunneling: sliced loaf clearly showing tunnels in the crumb
tunneling.caption: A long cavity under the crust, usually from trapped gas during shaping.

underproofed.caption: Not enough rise yet. Bake it now and you get a tight, dense crumb.

wheat-berry.caption: The whole kernel: bran outside, endosperm inside, germ at the base.

windowpane-test.alt: Windowpane Test: dough stretched thin and translucent between fingers
windowpane-test.caption: Stretch a piece of dough thin. If light shows through without it tearing, the gluten is developed.
